mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate cheaper capital.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive during FEDFUNDS declines (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate exceeding 5.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that trigger immediate equity sell-offs due to recession fears, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 5.5%, SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03) or t-test p > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate broad demand contraction that precedes equity market corrections, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: The combined HOUST and RSAFS decline signal fails to predict negative returns (Rank IC < 0.03) or positive returns occur in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, a sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals manufacturing slowdowns that reduce corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: During late-cycle expansion, INDPRO declines do not produce negative 20-day SPX returns (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) signals strong economic expansion that supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth does not correlate with positive 5-day SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03) or t-test p > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0%, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03) or t-test p > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicates severe labor market contraction that triggers immediate equity sell-offs, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The combined PAYEMS decline and UNRATE rise signal fails to predict negative returns (Rank IC < 0.03) or positive returns occur in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles, CPI inflation exceeding 3.0% annually signals persistent inflation that leads to further rate hikes, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days as real rates rise.
failure_condition: During monetary tightening cycles, CPIAUCSL > 3.0% does not produce negative 60-day SPX returns (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03.
